title: Repentance and the Davidic Model
english: Having attached himself to the sin of the world, being washed by the blood which is from his slaughter, he is whitened above a pillar. And the things concerning David have happened in a similar way; for he was led astray by a fleece (the blood of the typical sheep) and was washed by Jesus as if to be whitened above a pillar; and here he signifies a spiritual pillar.

Many times the doctrines and the powers of the soul are like bones; these are humbled by sin and by sophistic enchantment. But having heard the joy and gladness of God, the humbled bones will rejoice (Ps 50:10). And sins are erased from the transformation of virtues (Ps 50:11b); for just as knowledge coming into the soul erases and makes the ignorance vanish, so also every sin is erased by the presence of perfect virtue.

If you will erase all my sins, the ones written through the impressions in my heart, you create a pure heart in me, lacking all evil (Ps 50:12), but also kindle a steadfast spirit within my indwellings. And the upright thoughts and earnest perceptions dwelling in the soul are those about which he says: 'And all that is within me, bless his name.' And the steadfast spirit is the Holy Spirit or the conscience, the upright one, which the spirit of a man within him says. It is to be noted that what the voice has created does not signify essential beings, but a certain relationship being established which has been produced.

Of the earnest ones being unceasingly presented before the face of God, only the one sinning is cast out and rejected from him (Ps 50:13). But do not judge me, being contained by your divine comprehension, to be such a one as to be rejected from your face; but also do not take away the Holy Spirit whom you made to dwell in me, lest I be made naked of it (Ps 50:14). Expecting this descent of the Savior, by which it happens that he possesses perfect joy, he entreats the Father, saying: 'Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and with a ruling and perfect spirit support me.' And in these things, the Holy Spirit says 'ruling and leading' is either the man's internal principle or the soul of the man. And this ruling spirit desires support and confirmation according to the former interpretation.

We do not permit ourselves to ever overlook God, those who are diligent to do repentance and to demonstrate the teaching concerning repentance. Behold, indeed, even here what has been said is confirmed: for through the confession toward God, He promises to teach the lawless the ways of God himself, so that having stepped upon these, even if they were once impious, they might return to Him in a little while.

For those who have accomplished righteousness have the imitation and pattern of a good life, so also those who have erred concerning knowledge have to imitate the one coming into repentance, being impious ones returning toward God. 'Since by which I have done toward death, I am full of sins of blood' (Ps 50:16a), 'save me from these, the God who is once and our own.' Perhaps also David, from the sins of Uriah and if any others died with him, is worthy to be saved by God, being the God of his salvation.

'My tongue, called my own, in the always speaking concerning your righteousness, will rejoice in your righteousness' (Ps 50:17). From that, God opens the lips of the one having received the word in the opening of his mouth, so that his mouth shall proclaim the praises of God, always praising and giving thanks to Him.

'He who confesses concerning his own sin, what do you wish to discuss concerning Zion and Jerusalem?' (Ps 50:16b/20). But since we hope that he has not been entirely harmed by having stumbled in the short race, for this reason, possessing a prophetic thing and praying for and prophesying the communion of the Holy Spirit, [he says]: 'Doing good, saying that Zion was brought into being in your good pleasure for your son and approaching the Spirit'; but also the walls of Jerusalem are being built up. And these are guards of angels, a rooting out of incorruptible decrees.

He says righteousness, which is standing together through the faith of Jesus Christ for all those believing. But this righteousness turns out to be a lifting up and spiritual holocausts, and 'sacrifice a sacrifice of righteousness' (Ps 51:19); but also upon the spiritual altar, they bring up oxen like tillers, not other souls, but having been seen as the souls of martyrs, being brought up upon the heavenly altar.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Divine Providence and the Folly of Unbelief
english: Like the calves. For in the Revelation of John, the souls of those having been perfected through the name of Jesus and his testimony have been seen under the heavenly altar (Rev 6:9).

Who then is to provide a pretext for such a tragedy, he who is the shepherd of irrational animals? For we are without a leader. David, having realized his own great wickedness, spoke the words of the psalm (Ps 51) as if to the one moving him through envy, the devil, as if he were present.

Regarding the phrase 'The name of the Day let them reveal here,' it signifies the whole time according to which he errs. The words of 'drowning' are those bringing punishment, the drowning signifying chastisement, just as the lips of the unthinking drown him.

And the Edomite is not truly interpreted as earthly, always shaking because of being uncertain; for he is interpreted as being in a state of instability, he who, having worked slander against the healers of God, loved a deceitful tongue and with it words drowning him. And the Gospel signifies drowning to be the punishment, saying to the one causing scandal among the little ones in the church: 'It is better to be drowned in the depths of the sea' (Matt 18:6), with a millstone hung around his neck.

Because he loved evil to the end, he falls completely, as one not well built but also as one badly planted; 'Every planting which my heavenly Father has not planted shall be uprooted' (Matt 15:13); but he will be made to migrate from the holy tent, casting out and driving you away from that tent, whom you have slandered and into whom you have led to death, even the root of the living. For even if you were an Edomite, if you had attached yourself to Israel through the instruction of the law, you were planted in the tent and in the land of the living; for if you did not have reverence toward the God of Israel, you would not have even begun to disturb the sanctuary. And the things said against this man will apply to all those falling away from piety.
The very pious, those falling away from virtue into wickedness, receive a fear lest they themselves suffer the same. Nor will they dare to mock the fallen, as if saying they would laugh at him.

Thus a man does not set God as his helper; for he has not cast out his servants and attendants. Connect this to the fact that he who rejects you, rejects me. [Ps 51:11] Thanksgiving through confessing to God shows that he has done it, perhaps what he had previously set forth. For he had set forth to flee from Saul.

But also, 'what shall I do?' he says, 'your name is such that I might encounter whatever is good and full of goodness in the presence of your holy things'; [Ps 52:2a] for those having been made steadfast by the holiness of your goodness perceive it.

One is called foolish if he is lacking divine wisdom. For it appears that the word which does not preserve common sense is not about anything. For knowing that a thought of God has been cast upon every soul, embracing ungodliness, he is a god to no one except to his own heart. And thus the foolish devil does not act toward the heart of another (but his own is lying prostrate before God), but toward that which has become from him through sinning, he is a god to no one except to himself. [Ps 52:2b]

For he who has thought badly concerning God enters into wickedness; for casting out the piety of his own soul, he has also cast out with it all virtue following it like a royal garment of piety. Therefore, those saying through foolishness that God does not exist have corrupted their own mind by practicing lawlessness, from which they became loathsome, that is, they have become abominable. If it is chosen hereafter. [Ps 52:2c]
All those sinning, even those who seem to do good, not strictly and truly doing, but so that they might take a pattern of it through a mirror and an enigma, doing it himself. [Ps 52:2c]

The present verse introduces providence, of not only those in heaven but also those on earth; [Ps 52:3] for it has been said to look down providently from heaven upon the sons of men, not looking upon them from without only according to the body, but also according to the hidden part of the heart. He looks upon the sons of men, so that I might know if he is one who understands by doing the good and seeking God by examining the truth. And it has been said in a human way that he stoops from heaven to see if he understands; for great, if not in this way, is the impact.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Prayer of the Righteous and the Judgment of God
english: He has the knowledge of the hiding of all things (Ps 52:4). And from the present word we learn that sin consists in a transgression of the law by one who follows, if he is by nature evil. For all have turned aside; and this turning aside is sin, a failure not of the straight way. And those who turned aside were useless; saying [it is] useless, either according to the dominance of passions or according to the ignorance of one who, not thinking, is swept away into other things, does not have the knowledge of one thing. Of all those turning aside, it is rightly said, 'He does not do good' (Ps 52:5). According to each of the aforementioned, the 'until one' [limit] shows that neither is there one doing good, nor one not doing good.

Since wisdom will not enter a craftless soul, it must be known through divine knowledge. For it is not to be read according to a walk but according to a decision (Ps 52:6). There they will fear a fear that no fear can be brought up to the coming age; in that, fleeing from pain and sighing and grief, one must have courage. In this, not being in a state of fear, those approaching the things by which they will be punished will fear. Therefore, they will fear what God revealed there regarding those who became hypocrites, having the aim of pleasing men, scattering their bones, the doctrines and conveniences of laziness and greed, and the impulses of a vile soul. For if even there they were thought to be pleasing to men, deceiving [them], but being nullified by God as if they were nothing, they were shamed. And perhaps those doing evil will encounter the previously spoken-of punishments. But those hypocritically acting the part of virtue will not be tried by another punishment, their hypocrisy having been exposed; for he who does almsgiving to be glorified by men will not be punished by fire or anything of that kind (for he did not show mercy), but will be shamed, having been shown to have shared in the poverty of existing things not through God but through men (Ps 52:7). For sin is that which takes captive those who do it. But the forgiveness of sins being given as a gift, the [Lord] rejoices.

Israel and Jacob rejoice with those rejoicing in the heavens, similarly with one sinner repenting. Christ is the power of the Father. Since He judges the hidden things of men, He entreats that they be handed over for examination not to other judges, but by the power of the good God; for those, seeking forgiveness for those they passed over, will have vengeance happen against those who do the same thing in vain.

It is necessary that his prayer become well-pleasing and that he receive the things for which he prayed. But also, having become near to God through good works, 'Enlighten [with] the words of my mouth' (Ps 52:9). For no one, uttering a word that is idle, shameful, or some other evil, wants God to enlighten his words, but only everyone speaking the true and pious.

He says that those having an opposing disposition to the earnest ones are strangers, and the wicked demons are strong. And he says: because they did not set God before them, turning away from Him and having given their backs to Him, they rose up against the righteous and sought his soul.

He confesses God as a helper, perhaps the Father and Lord sustaining his soul, so that He might somehow turn the Son; 'He will turn the evils toward my enemies; for they desire to bring evil upon me' (Ps 53:6), these things He turns toward them, this being judged by the Lord in this way. 'Do to him as he has done to his neighbor' (Ps 55:23) agrees with this. And the truth of God, reproving those who are liars, destroys them if they are such; for they are not to be refuted at all, but rather they are such as the holy one prays.

Having these things happened, coming to thanksgiving with a self-willed mind, 'I will offer to You a voluntary sacrifice, not by necessity or force, but by a self-commanded readiness' (Ps 54:6). Lifting up a prayer to God, he entreats Him to draw near to him so that He may receive the prayer which he has brought forward through his trials. For He is near to the one saying, 'to receive the word.' And since I entreat, I do not take courage from another that the things lacking me will be replenished from You; do not despise the plea for which I entreat You. Give to me, [from those] lifting up holy hands without anger and...
